status: Unreviewed alternate actual-reference initial-point proof by bounded Tate normalization, explicit going-down and finite Gauss fibres

steps.title: Domain and proposed alternate initial-point lemma
steps.text: UNREVIEWED proposed alternative to the canonical-reduction/Poi initial-point chain in251. Let C be complete algebraically closed nontrivially real-valued of characteristic/residue characteristic0, R=C-degree ring, a a nonzero topologically nilpotent scalar. Suppose an ACTUAL proper flat formal model of the same smooth geometrically integral projective n-dimensional X_C is covered by finitely many a-adically complete R-flat charts S=R<T_1,...,T_m>/I with I finitely generated, and with actual generic analytic algebras B=S[1/a] geometrically smooth/pure dimensional n. Suppose its actual line bundle M is the pullback of the original embedding bundle by a finite normalization morphism, with the SAME generic bundle. These are hypotheses here, not a model-existence theorem. BE4.20 supplies a candidate actual normalized closure over algebraically closed C, but its generated normalization/completion applications must still be checked. The aim is a FINITE set Sigma of actual component points norming all same-bundle sections, with original generic support, value group equal to C and maximal residual dimension n, without claiming unique reduction fibres or equality of residual fields with component fields.

steps.title: Bounded division and preparation by contraction
steps.text: Write T_m=C<T_1,...,T_m> with multiplicative Gauss norm. For a nonzero nonunit f, divide by a scalar so its norm is1; its reduction is a nonzero finite polynomial. Choose integers N_i as distinct sufficiently separated powers of a base larger than all exponents appearing in this finite polynomial. The invertible bounded shear T_i -> T_i+T_m^{N_i} (i<m), with inverse subtraction, gives a unique highest T_m reduction monomial whose coefficient is a nonzero scalar. The corresponding leading coefficient is a unit in T_(m-1) of norm1 with bounded inverse. Dividing by it writes f=P+g where P is monic degree D in T_m with all lower coefficient norms<=1 and ||g||<1; D>0 since a reduction scalar would make f a unit. Polynomial long division by P gives linear quotient/remainder operators Q_0,R_0 of norm<=1 on polynomials. They extend to restricted series by completeness: truncation errors have Gauss norm tending to0. Remainders lie in the closed degree<D free T_(m-1)-module. For any h solve q=Q_0 h-Q_0(gq) by the convergent geometric contraction. Then h=fq+r with r=R_0(h-gq), degree<D; uniqueness follows from the same contraction. For h=T_m^D, Q_0h=1 and ||q-1||<1, so q is a bounded unit. The identity f q=T_m^D-r prepares f as a bounded unit times a monic polynomial of degree D with bounded coefficients. This gives both bounded division and preparation explicitly.

steps.title: Noetherianity, prime factors and normality of Tate algebras
steps.text: Induct on m, starting with C. For a nonzero ideal J in T_m choose f in J and shear/prepare as above. T_m/(f) is generated over the Noetherian T_(m-1) by 1,...,T_m^(D-1); hence J/(f), a submodule of this finite module, is finite. Its generators together with f generate J, so T_m is Noetherian. To prove factoriality, assume T_(m-1) is factorial. An irreducible f can be sheared/prepared to a monic bounded P. A polynomial factorization of monic P over the factorial base has monic factors. Multiplicativity of the polynomial Gauss norm forces both factor norms1, so every positive-degree monic factor has nonconstant reduction and is a nonunit in T_m. Thus irreducibility of f forces P irreducible in T_(m-1)[T_m]. It is prime there. Bounded division identifies T_m/(P) with T_(m-1)[T_m]/(P) as rings: every restricted series has its unique bounded polynomial remainder, and remainders multiply by polynomial reduction. This quotient is a domain, so f is prime in T_m. A Noetherian domain admits factorization into irreducibles by the ascending chain of principal ideals. Consequently all T_m are factorial, hence integrally closed. This avoids an appeal to regular-local-ring normality or the Tate Nullstellensatz for this step. Every transition between polynomial and restricted-series factors is an essential new assertion for independent review.

steps.title: Finite bounded normalization of the actual chart
steps.text: For the surjection T_m -> B, if its kernel is nonzero, choose a norm-one relation, shear and prepare it. The relation maps to0 in S as well because S is R-flat and injects into B; all shears and prepared coefficients are bounded, hence belong to the formal chart. The last formal generator satisfies an actual monic relation with bounded coefficients over the remaining coordinates. Reduce all restricted series by bounded division; the tail coefficients tend to0, so the resulting finite list of coefficients converges in the complete R<T_1,...,T_(m-1)>. Thus S is a finite module over the image of this smaller bounded algebra. Repeat for the kernel of the smaller Tate algebra mapping to B, until obtaining an injection T_d -> B with B finite over T_d and S finite over R_d=R<t_1,...,t_d>. This is a proof of bounded Noether normalization for this actual chart, not just algebraic integrality followed by an unjustified completion. Integral extensions preserve dimension by lying-over/going-up/incomparability. Induction using the same elimination shows dim T_d=d: coordinate prime chains give the lower bound; every nonzero prime quotient is finite over a Tate algebra with fewer variables and has dimension at most d-1. Since B is pure dimensional n, d=n. For each domain component B_i the contraction kernel in T_n is0, because a nonzero kernel would make its dimension at most n-1.

steps.title: Normality of the bounded base without Noetherianity
steps.text: The bounded ring R_n is exactly {h in T_n: ||h||_Gauss<=1}, and Frac(R_n)=Frac(T_n): each restricted series can be scaled by one nonzero C-scalar into R_n. An element h of this fraction field integral over R_n is integral over T_n, hence belongs to T_n by A3. Its monic integral equation and multiplicativity of the Gauss norm imply ||h||<=1: if ||h||>1 its leading power strictly dominates all other terms, a contradiction. Therefore h is in R_n. The base R_n is integrally closed although generally non-Noetherian. Its quotient by m_C R_n is k[t_1,...,t_n]: reduction is a finite polynomial because coefficients tend to0; if all coefficients reduce to0 their maximum is a scalar norm<1, so they are one scalar from m_C times a bounded series.

steps.title: Going-down proof in the required domain
steps.text: For integral domains A subset B with A normal and Frac(B)/Frac(A) finite separable, embed the latter in a finite normal closure E/F and let T be the integral closure of A in E. T is integral over both A and B. Lying-over follows by localization and the determinant/Nakayama argument in a finite integral subalgebra: 1 cannot lie in the maximal ideal times that finite algebra, so a maximal ideal above it exists. Going-up follows by quotienting a chosen prime and applying lying-over. Integral extensions have incomparability: after localization and quotient at a common contracted prime the domain is integral over a field and hence is a field. The finite normal-closure Galois group is transitive on primes of T over a fixed prime q of A. Otherwise, for primes P,Q over q with Q different from all conjugates of P, incomparability and finite prime avoidance give z in Q outside all conjugates of P. Explicit prime avoidance for incomparable P_i uses b_i in all P_j,j!=i but not P_i and z=sum a_i b_i, with a_i in Q but not P_i. The product of all Galois conjugates of z is invariant and integral, hence in A by normality. It belongs to Q and thus to q and P, but none of its factors belongs to P, contradiction. For q_0 subset q_1 and a chosen prime P_B over q_1, lift P_B to P_T. Choose a prime Q_0 over q_0 and go up to Q_1 over q_1 containing it. Conjugate Q_1 to P_T and intersect the conjugated Q_0 with B. This gives a prime below P_B contracting to q_0. No Noetherian or discrete-valuation hypothesis enters this going-down argument. Ordinary finite-field normal-closure and determinant lemmas are the explicit algebraic background.

steps.title: Every special component has dimension n
steps.text: Apply A6 to each domain component of the actual finite S over the normal R_n; its generic fraction extension is finite by A4 and characteristic0 gives separability. If S has several components, first handle the finitely many domain quotients; their Tate generic components dominate T_n by pure dimension, and R-flatness makes R_n inject into those components. Let p be minimal over m_C S and q its contraction to R_n, so q contains m_C R_n. Going down supplies p_0 subset p contracting exactly to m_C R_n. This p_0 contains m_C S, and minimality forces p_0=p. The residual component S/p is finite integral over k[t_1,...,t_n], and its fraction field has transcendence degree n. Thus every component of the actual chart special fibre has dimension n. If a minimal prime of S/p or a component decomposition is needed, check flatness/dominance on that component explicitly; no unsupported equidimensionality theorem is being substituted.

steps.title: Finite Gauss fibres are honest bounded analytic points
steps.text: Let eta be the unit Gauss point of the injected T_n. H(eta) contains Frac(T_n) isometrically, has residue k(t_1,...,t_n), and has the same value group as C. B tensor_(T_n) H(eta) is a finite algebra. Smoothness/reducedness and characteristic0 split its generic field algebras into a finite product of finite separable extensions of the complete field H(eta). Each such finite complete extension has a unique extended real valuation; the corresponding finite set Sigma_U consists of actual multiplicative seminorms on B. They are bounded on S: each original formal generator is integral over R_n by A4, and its monic bounded equation forces its value<=1; all restricted series then converge and are bounded by their formal Gauss norm. Hence these are actual points of the supplied formal chart, not arbitrary valuations on a replacement carrier. A generic formal-reduction point restricts exactly to the Gauss norm because A7 makes the coordinate reductions algebraically independent. Conversely any point of Sigma_U has this independent residue subfield. Its reduction is minimal over m_C S, by A7 and integral incomparability. Thus Sigma_U is exactly the set of points above the generic points of the formal special components, without assuming the fibres are singletons.

steps.title: Characteristic polynomials prove norming directly
steps.text: Write B as its finite product of normal domain components; the actual generic smooth affinoid domain supplies normality. Each component field E_i is finite over F=Frac(T_n). For f in B, f_i is integral over T_n, so all coefficients of its field characteristic polynomial lie in T_n: they are symmetric expressions in integral conjugates and belong to F, and T_n is normal. The product P(Z)=product_i P_i(Z) is monic and P(f)=0 in B. At any actual analytic point x, its coefficient values are bounded by their Gauss norms, so the elementary non-Archimedean root bound gives |f(x)|<=max_j ||a_j||_Gauss^(1/j). This bound equals the largest absolute value of a root over the algebraic closure of H(eta): elementary symmetric coefficients give one inequality, and leading-term dominance gives the converse. The roots are the values of f on the finite Gauss fibre Sigma_U, because base change of the generic component fields to H(eta) has precisely those finite extension factors. Therefore sup_U |f|=max_(Sigma_U)|f|. This is norming for EVERY analytic function, obtained without canonical-reduction generic-fibre uniqueness. Finite sets and maximal coefficients here concern actual algebras and fields; no substitute inverse measure is introduced.

steps.title: Original generic support and maximal residual dimension
steps.text: Every H(x),x in Sigma_U, is finite over H(eta). Independent residue lifts are linearly independent over the base field after maximal-coefficient normalization, hence its residue field is finite algebraic over k(t_1,...,t_n). Thus s(x)=n. The value group extension has finite index; C has divisible value group, so an ordered real finite-index extension adds no values. To establish generic support in ORIGINAL X, approximate n independent unit residues in H(x) by elements of the scheme residue field kappa(x) with error<1; this is possible by the defining completion of a valued scheme point. Any polynomial relation over C, after normalizing a largest coefficient and reducing, would contradict independence of these residues. Hence trdeg_C kappa(x)>=n. Since X_C is integral dimensional n, the support is its generic point. This argument comes BEFORE any identification H(x) with a completion of C(X); it proves the necessary original function-field embedding.

steps.title: A finite global norming set and the original residue coordinates
steps.text: Take the union Sigma of the finite Sigma_U for finitely many actual formal charts trivializing M. The actual integral frame norm is1; a section of kM is an analytic function in that frame. A9 therefore norms EVERY section on the same actual bundle by Sigma. Each point reduces to a generic component Y. Since the normalized projective model is finite over the original schematic closure, Y maps finitely onto its component image Z; by A7 both have dimension n and k(Y) is finite over k(Z). The original projective coordinate ratios on any nonvanishing original S0 generate k(Z), which injects into H(x)-tilde by the reduction kernel. Their residue SUBFIELD consequently has transcendence degree n. Choose one ORIGINAL-field coefficient row for S0 nonzero at all finitely many Y: each bad set is a proper linear subspace of the infinite residue field vector space, because the original sections generate M. Lift a row with a unit entry to an invertible matrix over the original valuation ring. Its matrix and inverse are integral, so maxima of the original and changed section families agree at EVERY point. Then all original coordinate ratios have norm<=1 and S0 has norm1 at every x in Sigma. This supplies exactly the initial same-reference hypotheses for the common-curve/degree-slope argument252. No individual component point is claimed to norm all sections by itself.

steps.title: Genuine MA support and exact remaining obligations
steps.text: Whole CLDv1 6.5.1/6.6.8 identifies the residual germ and actual formal bundle with the reduction closure. At a nongeneric reduction that closure has dimension<n. Whole6.9.2, using6.8.3, makes the genuine n-fold curvature vanish there. Therefore actual MA(theta_C) is supported on the finite Sigma above generic reductions; O supplies positive coefficients with raw total V. Together with the preserved-section curve degree/slope argument this yields the prospective moment bound M0=V*a*D0, without exact component coefficients or residual-field equality. This whole alternate route is NEW and UNREVIEWED: no original closure or new accepted paper. Essential inputs still include the existence/completion properties of the actual normalized closure (BE4.18-4.20 in their algebraically closed domain), generic analytic smoothness/normality of its chart algebras, strict Tate fibre identifications, the complete classical valuation extension and field-degree facts, CLD support applications and every252 common-curve/slope step. The norm-preserving preparation/elimination and factorization proof must be independently checked; they are not supplied grants. This record neither proves arbitrary target attainment nor every-point uniqueness, and is not sent as hot feedback to active197/199.
